grades: High school sophomores and juniors (rising juniors and seniors)
name: Georgia Governor's Honors Program (GHP)
org: Georgia Governor's Office of Education, Workforce and Strategy (GOEWS)
city: Georgia (summer residential campus; host campus not named on the page read)
what_you_do: This is a mid-summer residential program on a college campus. It is for talented sophomores and juniors. Students study an area they were nominated in. It can be a subject, an art or a career field.
who_can_apply: Skilled and talented high school sophomores and juniors. A Georgia public school district, independent school or state charter school must nominate you. Home school students go through their local school district.
pay_detail: Free to apply. The page says required costs are travel to the semifinalist event and the host campus, basic supplies and optional spending money. Meals and rooms are provided.
deadline_text: Local school selection runs August to early November (ask your school's GHP Coordinator now). Then nominees get the online application link Nov 13, info session Dec 3, application due Jan 8, semifinalists told Feb 5. The page shows weekdays but no year; they match 2026 to 2027. Confirm with GHP.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply directly. Ask your school counselor or GHP Coordinator to nominate you. Nominees then complete an online application with a parent permission form, a recommendation and a transcript. GHP project manager: (404) 444-7062.
notes: Local nomination dates differ by school district and the page says they run August to early November, so move fast. Standardized test results are no longer required. The application page is marked updated 08/2026.
